messages.author: 1f4b75a9cfab7c26
messages.subject: Pango-Warning means "out of memory"?
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I'm experiencing problems with aroma.affymetrix on a linux 64bit
system. I suppose this a memory problem although the error message
sounds strange. Here is a short discription of the problem first
followed by the session info:

Symptom: Calculation abort during ChromosomeExplorer procedure with
cbs object.

Message:

> 20081126 20:09:32| Pathname: reports/MK_pancreas/ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY /GenomeWideSNP_6/cbs/panc_5061norm,chr16,x0128.png
> 20081126 20:09:32| Dimensions: 34658x400
> 20081126 20:09:32| Ticks by: 0.010000
> 20081126 20:09:32| Plotting graph...

> (process:17823): Pango-WARNING **: Invalid UTF-8 string passed to pango_layout_set_text()
> No fonts found; this probably means that the fontconfig
> library is not correctly configured. You may need to
> edit the fonts.conf configuration file. More information
> about fontconfig can be found in the fontconfig(3) manual
> page and on http://fontconfig.org

Observations:
1. The problem always occured until now when processing png files with
resolutions of 128.
2. The problem is independet of the dataset. I checked three different
data sets including the hapmap samples set used in the vignette.
3. The problem seems to appear when nearly the same amount of data has
been processed. Processing the three datasets he stop twice at
chromosome 16 (x128.png) and one on chromosome 15 (x128.png) of the
second sample. So he is finishing one sample without problems and
suddenly stops within the second.
4. The problem is reproduceable. Recalculating the first of my
datasets stop at the same point as before.
5. I had a similar problem under windows. Only there he aborted
calculation telling me that he doesn't have enough memory. The linux
system however should have enough memory provided.

Although the message doesn't sound like a moemoy prolem I supppose it
is one. Why should he otherwise always stop after processing nearly
the same amount of data?

Last two notes:

a) When I have look at the created 128 resolutions they are empty.
They do have a size of maybe around 25-30 kb. But all the picture
includes is the frame but no datapoints. Sometimes that is the same
for the x64 resolutions. Then the files are smaller in size than the
next smaller resolution file.

b) Windows dind't even calculate my x128 resolutions. He just made it
to the x64, processed some samples and died later becuase of lack of
memory. Why that? The ChromosomeExplorer function doesn't seem to have
a flag for selecting the desired resolutions to be ploted.

regards,

Benjamin

5.

Never heard of "Pango" before, but updating to the latest R *v2.8.0
patched* version *may* solve the problem, cf. thread 'Update on
reported issues with generating PNGs using the built-in cairo device'
on Nov 26, 2008:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/a84898f367c77389

>
> Observations:
> 1. The problem always occured until now when processing png files with
> resolutions of 128.
> 2. The problem is independet of the dataset. I checked three different
> data sets including the hapmap samples set used in the vignette.
> 3. The problem seems to appear when nearly the same amount of data has
> been processed. Processing the three datasets he stop twice at
> chromosome 16 (x128.png) and one on chromosome 15 (x128.png) of the
> second sample. So he is finishing one sample without problems and
> suddenly stops within the second.
> 4. The problem is reproduceable. Recalculating the first of my
> datasets stop at the same point as before.
It is not clear from this latter point if you restart R as well.

> 5. I had a similar problem under windows. Only there he aborted
> calculation telling me that he doesn't have enough memory. The linux
> system however should have enough memory provided.
>
> Although the message doesn't sound like a moemoy prolem I supppose it
> is one. Why should he otherwise always stop after processing nearly
> the same amount of data?

It is most likely related to the PNG device driver, which probably
cannot cope with cumulative amount data thrown at it.

The following threads reports similar problems and how they were
solved it by "forcing" another PNG driver:

1) Thread 'R crashing during CNV analysis', Nov 11-20, 2008:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/9853243d78fabf2

2) Thread 'ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks' on Aug 18-20, 2008:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/e06bc012b5359dea

>
> Last two notes:
>
> a) When I have look at the created 128 resolutions they are empty.
> They do have a size of maybe around 25-30 kb. But all the picture
> includes is the frame but no datapoints. Sometimes that is the same
> for the x64 resolutions. Then the files are smaller in size than the
> next smaller resolution file.

This indicate that the PNG device was opened and the plot was setup,
but then the error occurred, the plotting function was interrupted
with a guaranteed dev.off() (via on.exit()) at the end.

The same symptom has been reported by others when there has been
problems with the PNG device driver.

>
> b) Windows dind't even calculate my x128 resolutions. He just made it
> to the x64, processed some samples and died later becuase of lack of
> memory. Why that? The ChromosomeExplorer function doesn't seem to have
> a flag for selecting the desired resolutions to be ploted.

It is hard to tell without knowing how many arrays have been processed
before. But again, make sure to run the latest R v2.8.0 patched.
That can certainly be the solution.

How to change the 'zooms', see thread 'ChromosomeExplorer options' on
Jun 23-Jul 7, 2008:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/659debcf014702a

Let us know if and how this helped

Henrik
